title: Cousin Willie Bontemps passed off as his uncle
summary: Marge prompts the story of his cousin Willie Bontemps, Aunt Carrie's son, called his uncle because married women could not teach school. Willie played bass, guitar and banjo and took Zutty to rehearsals.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And your cousin was a big influence on you.
What is that?
Your cousin, I say he was a big influence on you.
Yes, he was. Well I used to call him my uncle. You know like we told you before,
because when you taught school, you see, my mother and my Aunt Carrie and my Uncle Willie, they were supposed to be brothers and sisters, you know.
But who was Willie actually, your cousin?
He really was my cousin, yes. But during that time if you were married you couldn't teach school, you know. And so that's why Willie became my uncle, you see?
He was your Aunt Carrie's son, was he?
That's right.
I see. How much older than you was he?
Oh, he was about 7 or 8 years older than I.
That was a lot.
Yes.
When you're a kid.
Why sure.
And what was his second name?
Bontemps.
Oh yes.
BON....
TEMPS?
TEMPS, that's right, yes. And he used to take me to different rehearsals, you know.
What did he play?
He played bass and guitar. And banjo.
This was after you'd gone to St. Louis, to New Orleans?
